Rashi on Niddah 45b:10:1.english: The matters stated, etc. - For a boy is quicker to mature intellectually than a girl.

Rashi on Niddah 45b:16:1.hebrew: לעונשין - וכגון דאייתי שתי שערות תוך הזמן, דאי לא אייתי — אפילו לאחר זמן לאו בר עונשין הוא; ולאחר זמן, אי אייתי ב' שערות — הוי גדול ובר עונשין:
Rashi on Niddah 45b:16:1.english: With regard to punishments - And [this is] in a case where he developed two [pubic] hairs during the time; for if he did not develop [them], even after the time he is not subject to punishment, and after the time, if he developed two hairs, he is an adult and subject to punishment.

Rashi on Niddah 45b:16:2.hebrew: כלפני הזמן - ולא ענשינן ליה, ושתי שערות הויא להו שומא:
Rashi on Niddah 45b:16:2.english: As before the time - And we do not punish him, and the two hairs are [considered] a mole.

Rashi on Niddah 45b:17:1.hebrew: וזאת לפנים - וזאת לשון נקבה, כלומר: רב חנינא, דשמיה לשון נקבה, אמר לפנים, כלומר: לפני זמן, ולא תטעה להחליף דבריהם. ל"א: שמו של רב, דאמר כלפני הזמן, מובלע בתיבת בישראל:
Rashi on Niddah 45b:17:1.english: Now this was in former times - "Vezot" is in the feminine form; that is to say, Rav Ḥanina, whose name is in the feminine form, said "in former times," meaning before the time, so that you do not err by switching their statements. Another explanation: The name of Rav, who said "as before the time," is embedded in the word beYisrael.

Rashi on Niddah 45b:18:1.hebrew: מתיב רב המנונא - קס"ד, כדאמר לקמן, דרב המנונא משנה יתירה דייק, דלא איצטריך למתנייה כדפרכינן לעיל. והא דתני ליה תנא דמתני' — למידק מינה לענין עונשין: הא תוך הזמן כלפני הזמן; דאי לענין נדרים, לא כלפני זמן ולא כלאחר זמן:
Rashi on Niddah 45b:18:1.english: Rav Hamnuna raises an objection - It enters our mind [to think], as [the Gemara] says later, that Rav Hamnuna inferred from a superfluous [clause in the] mishna, which did not need to be taught, as we asked above. And that which the tanna of the mishna taught it [was] to infer from it with regard to punishments: Behold, during the time [it is] like before the time; for if [it were] with regard to vows, [during the time is] neither like before the time nor like after the time.

Rashi on Niddah 45b:1:1.hebrew: לכשיגדיל יבעול - והך ביאה הוי קנין גמור, ואם בא לגרשה אינה צריכה חליצה, דכתיב (דברים כ״ה:ה׳) ולקחה לו לאשה — כיון שלקחה, נעשית כאשתו לכל דבר:
Rashi on Niddah 45b:1:1.english: When he reaches majority he shall engage in intercourse - And this act of intercourse is a complete acquisition; and if he comes to divorce her, she does not require ḥalitza, as it is written (Deuteronomy 25:5): "and take her to him as a wife" — once he has taken her, she becomes like his wife in all matters.

Rashi on Niddah 45b:21:1.hebrew: מגופא דמתני' דייק - דלא מתוקמא אלא כשהביא שתי שערות, ואפ"ה לא חשיב ליה גדול עד לאחר זמן. והשתא ליכא למיפרך: לידוק מרישא, דהא לא דייק מידי, דבין רישא ובין סיפא לגופא איצטריך לענין נדרים, דלא תימא: הני מילי היכא דלא קאמרי אינהו, אבל היכא דאמרי אינהו כו', כדאמר לעיל. ומיהו מגופא דסיפא שמעינן, דעד דמטו לאחר זמן בעינן יודע להפלות; ואם אינו יודע להפלות, ואפילו הביא ב' שערות - לאו איש הוא, דניהוי נדרו נדר מחמת אישות בלא הפלאה:
Rashi on Niddah 45b:21:1.english: He infers from the body of the mishna - For it can only be established [as referring to a case] where he developed two hairs, and even so, [the mishna] does not consider him an adult until after that time. And now, one cannot object: "Let him infer from the first clause," for he is not inferring anything [from superfluous phrasing], as both the first clause and the latter clause are needed for their own sake regarding the matter of vows, so that you should not say: "These matters apply where they do not state [anything], but where they do state [that they know or do not know], etc.," as [the Gemara] stated above. However, from the body of the latter clause itself we learn that until they reach after that time, we require [that he] know how to articulate [a vow with discernment]; and if he does not know how to articulate [it], and even if he developed two hairs, he is not a man [i.e., an adult], such that his vow would be a [valid] vow by virtue of adulthood without articulation.

Rashi on Niddah 45b:21:2.hebrew: קטן הוא - ואמאי נדרו נדר? הא לאו בחזקת גדול הוא כל זמן שלא הביא ב' שערות, ומופלא סמוך לאיש נמי לא הוי, דהא אינו יודע לשם מי נדר, ומהיכא תיתי דנדרו נדר:
Rashi on Niddah 45b:21:2.english: He is a minor - And why should his vow be a [valid] vow? For he is not presumed to be an adult as long as he has not developed two hairs, and he is also not a mufla samukh le'ish [a discerning minor close to adulthood], for he does not know in Whose name he vowed. And from where would it be derived that his vow is a [valid] vow?

Rashi on Niddah 45b:21:3.hebrew: אלא לאו כשהביא - ומשום הכי נדרו נדר, אע"ג דאין יודע להפלות, דהא גדול הוא:
Rashi on Niddah 45b:21:3.english: Rather, is it not when he developed [two hairs] - And that is why his vow is a [valid] vow, even though he does not know how to articulate [a vow with discernment], for he is an adult.

Rashi on Niddah 45b:2:1.english: Are examined - [To see] whether she knew in Whose name she vowed and in Whose name she consecrated.

Rashi on Niddah 45b:4:1.hebrew: קודם הזמן הזה - כגון בתינוקת קודם שיבא ראש השנה של שתים עשרה, ובתינוק קודם ראש השנה של שלש עשרה:
Rashi on Niddah 45b:4:1.english: Prior to this time - For example, in [the case of] a girl, before the beginning of the twelfth year arrives, and in [the case of] a boy, before the beginning of the thirteenth year.

Rashi on Niddah 45b:4:2.english: Their vows are not vows - For they are minors.

Rashi on Niddah 45b:4:3.hebrew: אחר הזמן הזה - בתינוקת מבת שתים עשרה ויום אחד ולמעלה, בתינוק מי"ג שנה ויום אחד ולמעלה:
Rashi on Niddah 45b:4:3.english: After this time - In the case of a girl, from twelve years and one day old and above; in the case of a boy, from thirteen years and one day old and above.

Rashi on Niddah 45b:4:4.hebrew: אפילו אמרו אין אנו יודעין כו' - גדולים הם, ובכלל שוטה נמי לא מחזקינן להו, דסופו לבא לכלל דעת, ואין שוטה אלא המקרע כסותו, והלן בבית הקברות, והיוצא יחידי בלילה. אבל תוך הזמן הזה, אם יודע לשם מי נדר הוי נדר, ואם לאו לא הוי נדר, דקטן הוא. ובגמרא מפרש כולה מילתא:
Rashi on Niddah 45b:4:4.english: Even if they said: "We do not know," etc. - They are adults, and we also do not presume them to be in the category of an imbecile, for [a person] is destined to attain mental competence, and one is not [considered] an imbecile unless [he is] one who tears his garment, one who sleeps in a cemetery, and one who goes out alone at night. However, during this time, if he knows in Whose name he vowed, it is a [valid] vow; and if not, it is not a [valid] vow, for he is a minor. And in the Gemara the entire matter is explained.

Rashi on Niddah 45b:5:1.english: Why do I [need this]? - Naturally I know that from here on, she does not require examination.

Rashi on Niddah 45b:5:2.hebrew: סד"א בודקין לעולם - והאי דקתני בת אחת עשרה נבדקין, למעוטי קודם זמן הזה, דלא בדקינן ליה, דאפילו ידע קטן הוא. קמ"ל דלמעוטי אחר זמן נמי אתא:
Rashi on Niddah 45b:5:2.english: It might enter your mind to say that we examine forever - And [as for] that which [the mishna] teaches, "A girl of eleven years, [her vows] are examined," [it is] to exclude [the period] before this time, when we do not examine her, for even if she knows [to Whom she vowed], she is a minor. [Therefore,] it teaches us that it came to exclude [the period] after [this] time as well.

Rashi on Niddah 45b:6:1.hebrew: בודקין כל י"ב למה לי - הא תנא דמיום א' בשתים עשרה מתחילין לבדוק, ואינן קיימין בלא בדיקה עד יום אחד בי"ג, אלמא כל י"ב הוי זמן בדיקה:
Rashi on Niddah 45b:6:1.english: "One examines throughout the twelfth [year]," why do I need [this]? - Behold, [the Tanna] taught that from day one of the twelfth [year] one begins to examine [her vows], and they are not in effect without examination until day one of the thirteenth [year]; consequently, the entire twelfth [year] is the time of examination.

Rashi on Niddah 45b:6:2.english: Where we examined [her for] thirty days - The first [thirty days] of the twelfth [year].

Rashi on Niddah 45b:6:3.english: And she did not know how to clearly utter [a vow] - To specify for Whose Name she vowed. And [the Gemara] adopted the language of the verse: "When [one] clearly utters a vow" [Numbers 6:2].

Rashi on Niddah 45b:6:4.english: We should not examine further - And let us presume her to be a minor.

Rashi on Niddah 45b:7:1.hebrew: בת י"א כו' למה לי - מדתנן ליה בודקין כל י"ב, שמעינן דמקמי הכי לא:
Rashi on Niddah 45b:7:1.english: A girl of eleven, etc., why do I need [it] - Since it taught: "One examines throughout the entire twelfth [year]," we deduce that prior to this, [she is] not [examined].

Rashi on Niddah 45b:9:1.hebrew: הני מילי - דמקמי הכי מוחזקין קטנים, ולאחר זמן מוחזקין גדולים:
Rashi on Niddah 45b:9:1.english: These matters - That prior to this they are presumed to be minors, and after [this] time they are presumed to be adults.

Rashi on Niddah 45b:9:2.hebrew: היכא דלא קאמרי אינהו - קודם הזמן יודעין אנו, ולאחר זמן אין אנו יודעין:
Rashi on Niddah 45b:9:2.english: Where they do not say - Prior to the time, "We know," and after the time, "We do not know."

Tosafot on Niddah 45b:10:1.hebrew: אלו דברי רבי - נראה דהלכה כרבי, דלקמן בפירקין אמרי' כל י"ב שנה ממאנת, ומכאן ואילך אינה ממאנת. ובפ' נערה שנתפתתה (כתובות ד' נא.) אמר דהלכה כרבי לגבי רשב"א, לבד מלגבי מילתא דהתם. וביש נוחלין (ב"ב דף קכד:) נמי פסיק הלכה כרבי מחבירו:
Tosafot on Niddah 45b:10:1.english: These are the words of Rabbi - It appears that the halakha follows Rabbi, for later in our chapter we say: "Throughout all twelve years she may refuse [her marriage], and from this point onward she may not refuse." And in the chapter [entitled] *Na'arah She-Nitpateta* (Ketubot 51a), [the Gemara] states that the halakha follows Rabbi against Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar, except with regard to the matter [discussed] there. And in *Yesh Nochalin* (Bava Batra 124b) as well, it rules: The halakha follows Rabbi against his colleague.

Tosafot on Niddah 45b:13:1.hebrew: שהתינוק מצוי בבית רבו - ואפילו אין לו רב, רגיל לצאת ולבא, ומתפקח יותר:
Tosafot on Niddah 45b:13:1.english: Since a boy is frequently in his teacher's house - And even if he does not have a teacher, he is accustomed to go out and come in, and becomes more discerning.

Tosafot on Niddah 45b:15:1.hebrew: אילימא לנדרים - ובלא הביא ב' שערות, ואפ"ה נדרו נדר אם ידע למי נדר, כיון שהוא שנה לפני גדלות, דמסתמא יביא ב' שערות כשיהיה בן י"ג ויום אחד, כדאמר רבא לקמן: חזקה הביאה שערות:
Tosafot on Niddah 45b:15:1.english: If we say [it is] regarding vows - And [this is] without having brought two hairs, and even so his vow is a vow if he knew to Whom he vowed, since it is a year before adulthood, for presumably he will bring two hairs when he is thirteen years and one day old, as Rava says below: "There is a presumption that she brought hairs."

Tosafot on Niddah 45b:16:1.hebrew: אלא לענין עונשין - וכגון שהביא ב' שערות תוך הזמן, מי חשיב גדול כמו לאחר זמן לענין חליצה וקדושין, ונדרים לקיים נדרו אפי' אינו יודע למי נדר, כיון שהביא ב' שערות; ומיבעיא ליה אי הוי שומא אי לאו:
Tosafot on Niddah 45b:16:1.english: Rather, with regard to punishments - And [this is a case] where he grew two [pubic] hairs during the time: Is he considered an adult just like after the time—regarding ḥalitza, betrothal (kiddushin), and vows, to uphold his vow even if he does not know to Whom he vowed—since he grew two hairs? And the dilemma being raised is whether [the hairs] are [considered merely] a mole (shuma) or not.

Tosafot on Niddah 45b:9:1.hebrew: קודם הזמן הזה למה לי סד"א כו' - וא"ת: ובת י"א שנה, למה ליה למימר דאילו חריפא לא בדקינן לה, דהיינו קודם הזמן? ויש לומר, דזו אף זו קתני: דלא מיבעיא דלא אמרי, אלא אפילו אמרי לא מהני:
Tosafot on Niddah 45b:9:1.english: Prior to this time, why do I need [it]? It might enter your mind to say, etc. - And if you say: And [as for the clause of] "a girl of eleven years", why did [the Tanna] need to state [it, to teach] that if she is sharp we do not examine her, which is [the period of] "prior to the time"? And one can say that [the Tanna] taught [in the manner of] "not only this, but that" (zu af zu): for it is not necessary [to state that where] they did not say [that they know], but even [where] they said [that they know], it is of no avail.
